newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: France sends police to riot-torn Guiana.
newsitem.headline: France sends police to riot-torn Guiana.

text.p: French police flew into riot-torn French Guiana on Wednesday after a second wave of violence in six months shook the capital Cayenne, officials said.
Violence erupted late on Tuesday for the second time in a week when demonstrators and police clashed after the arrest of three more members of the territory's independence movement.
Jean Ballandras, a senior French official in France's South American department, said on radio more than 150 policemen had arrived from mainland France in the last few days.
"Their mission will be to...control the city centre," he said.
Police started firing tear gas grenades to disperse crowds on Tuesday. They clashed with armed bands of hooded youths throughout the night.
Groups of demonstrators set fire to tyres and one shop was sacked. There were no reports of injuries.
There have been no reports of violence in the territory's city of Kourou where The European Space Agency (ESA) Ariane rocket launch site is located.
Earlier on Tuesday police arrested Jean-Victor Castor and Fabien Canavy both members of the Guiana Workers Union (UTG).
Jean-Claude Ringuet, a member of the Guiana National Popular Party (PNPG), gave himself up after taking refuge for several hours in Cayenne's town hall.
French officials pledged last week to crack down on violence in French Guiana after violence last Thursday left two policemen wounded and several shops sacked.
The latest unrest was triggered by a series of arrests, including that of Alain Michel a founding member of the PNPG.

He was charged with arson and violence against a magistrate when the residence of French Guiana's state prosecutor was attacked last November in a previous wave of riots in which one person was killed and property worth millions of dollars was damaged.

French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America, is the only non-independent territory on the mainland of the Western Hemisphere. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
